articles.title: Only 15% of People Are Truly Self-Aware
articles.description:
#DataScience #CommunicationSkills #SoftSkills

Gilbert Eijkelenboom bestselling author of People Skills for Analytical Thinkers and founder of the training firm MindSpeaking joins @JonKrohnLearns to make the case that communication is a core data skill, not an optional extra. Gilbert shares the “And, But, Therefore” framework for turning dense analysis into a story stakeholders act on, the research suggesting only around 15% of people are genuinely self-aware (and how journaling, meditation, and exercise help close that gap), how childhood experiences install behavioral “algorithms” we carry into the workplace and why behavior change precedes attitude change, so doing small, uncomfortable things for 30 days can rewire how you see yourself.

This episode is brought to you by: 
• Anthropic: https://claude.ai/superdata
• Acceldata: https://www.acceldata.io
• Gurobi: https://www.superdatascience.com/gurobi
• Notion: http://notion.com/superdata

Interested in sponsoring a SuperDataScience Podcast episode? Email natalie@superdatascience.com for sponsorship information.

In this episode you will learn:
• (00:00:00) Introduction
• (00:02:54) Why your analysis only creates value once people actually use it
• (00:24:53) What it really means that only ~15% of people are self-aware
• (00:34:01) The “And, But, Therefore” framework for data storytelling
• (00:37:51) How childhood installs personal “algorithms”
• (00:48:13) Why behavior change comes before attitude change
• (00:52:18) Defusing the trigger between data teams and pushy stakeholders

Additional materials: https://www.superdatascience.com/1005
